correctness.rationale: Every non-cut vertex of a connected block graph is simplicial and cannot be internal on any geodesic. If a dual set contains a cut vertex c, the selected-geodesic condition permits selected vertices in at most one component of G-c; the dual condition permits unselected vertices in at most one component. The component partition forces exactly two pure sides, X=V(C) union {c}. A nonclique selected side has two nonadjacent selected endpoints and a geodesic with an internal selected point, contradiction. Hence the selected side is one pendant clique block with c in exactly two blocks; conversely its clique and the convex remaining component satisfy both conditions. Sets are disjoint, giving the enumerator and hereditary iff criterion. Independently constructed BFS-and-block-decomposition checker verified 4943 block graphs and 414102 vertex subsets, including every connected labeled block graph of order <=6. Finite checks supplement the general proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2024 dual-position paper provides convexity and the simplicial-subset lower bound plus maximum values for block graphs, but not a complete necessary-and-sufficient enumeration of all dual sets on arbitrary block graphs or an exact criterion for hereditary failure. Earlier ordinary and later edge/graph-product results differ in variant or coverage; indexed records of complete multipartite and square-page book graphs are not stronger coverage. Special complete graphs and known path maximum-set cases are explicitly excluded from novelty. Full publication priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Search cannot exclude undiscovered or inaccessible equivalent work, especially a separate paper enumerating dual convex-position sets in block graphs.
Record-level search-result summaries are not substitutes for full linked articles; comparisons to those records are restricted to supported summarized claims.
A classical structural formula could be known under convexity or general-position aliases outside queried terminology.

value.rationale: This complete natural size enumerator of a graph-position invariant answers a defined all-subsets counting question across every connected block graph, beyond existing extremal parameters. The correction polynomial has a direct graph-structural interpretation; its coefficients recover the full size profile of qualified pendant blocks. The hereditary iff criterion characterizes exactly when the dual-set family fails downward closure, a phenomenon emphasized by the foundational 2024 theory. It is a global structural classification and not a small isolated numerical recomputation.
